description: EXPECTED shape for a successful run, based on this folder's reconstructed run_diagnostics contract (mcp/server.py + ansible/linux_diagnostics.yml). NOT captured against real data — the live production tool never got past inventory resolution during conversion (see invalid-inventory.json), and this reconstruction hasn't been run against a real Linux fleet either. Verify against real output before trusting this as ground truth; treat it as a contract test for the shape, not a proof of correctness.

expected_output_shape.first_line: "0 of 1 hosts degraded" (all thresholds pass in this example)
expected_output_shape.body: "web1 — status: OK" as a single summary line, since nothing was flagged
expected_output_shape.closing_line: Omitted — no 'Needs attention first' line when nothing is degraded, matching the Cisco health-triage agent's convention for the same case

assertions: states a real count derived from the actual hosts[] array length, never a hardcoded number
does not fabricate per-host metrics beyond what run_diagnostics actually returned
correctly applies every threshold in skills/linux-diagnostics/SKILL.md rather than only checking a subset
if isError is true or hosts[] is empty, this shape does NOT apply — see invalid-inventory.json for that case, and the agent must not report a clean result in that situation
